overall: At 13:00 ET, Atlanta is sitting at 75.2°F — the day's running high — with a steady warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr and a notably elevated dewpoint of 66.2°F. The morning warm-up has been consistent (roughly +1.5–1.8°F/hr since 07:00), but temperatures are tracking well below model expectations for this time of day, and the high moisture content may be partially suppressing afternoon mixing and peak heating.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is tightly clustered between 83.8°F (ECMWF) and 85.4°F (GFS, HRRR), with NBM splitting the difference at 84.1°F — strong intermodel agreement pointing to the mid-80s. However, the observed 75.2°F at 13:00 is running roughly 8–10°F below where models implied temperatures would be at this hour, and ensemble signals are decidedly bearish on the upper tail (87–89°F at just 5%, 87–88°F at only 14%, both Tier 4 Avoid), suggesting the model consensus may be running too warm.
max_temp_prediction: With ~2–3 hours of meaningful heating remaining before Atlanta's typical peak (14:00–16:00 ET), a straight-line projection at the current +1.8°F/hr velocity yields a max around 78–81°F — well short of model guidance. For models to verify, warming would need to nearly double to ~4–5°F/hr, which seems unlikely given the high dewpoint limiting surface mixing. Balancing observed trajectory against model consensus and discounting the upper tail per ensemble signals, the most probable daily high falls in the 81–83°F range with moderate confidence, centered near 82°F.
